findings.text: Parent stop and continue reporting chooses its target from tracing context, using the immediate parent for tracer reports and otherwise resolving through the group leader toward its real parent. Each report carries child identity and ownership viewed from parent namespaces alongside accumulated processor times plus a reason distinguishing continued, stopped and trapped transitions with matching status derivation.

Child status signal generation is suppressed when recipient disposition ignores the child signal or disables stop reports, while waiter wakeup proceeds in all cases. Disposition inspection, possible queued delivery and wakeup share one atomic handler locked region.

Exit accounting broadcast is skipped when the reporting family is unavailable or no listener exists. A solitary exiting task yields one process record, while group termination with existing group storage yields an added group aggregate with completion marking and current version stamping.

Message buffer setup reserves space for future attributes and treats unsolicited broadcasts differently from request replies by consuming a per CPU sequence for the former. Failures in allocation or header placement leave no buffer behind and report an error.

Listener distribution finalizes the message a single time, then provides each recipient except the last with a cloned copy and unicasts individually. Refused recipients are flagged during shared protected traversal and unlinked later under exclusive protection, while clone exhaustion ends the walk and discards any remainder.

Per task record assembly begins from cleared storage, applies the current version, preserves context switch counts, and composes delay data plus basic, extended and executable sections through separate helpers.
Executable identity capture samples device and inode numbers from a held executable reference and otherwise records zeros. Any held reference is released after sampling.

Executable lookup is offered at task granularity and at address space granularity. Task level access excludes kernel threads and stabilizes the address space under task protection, while address space level access uses read side protection. Both transfer a new reference to the caller or report absence with null.

Basic accounting population provides elapsed times for task and group, wall clock birth estimates with bounded clamping, flag derivation from exit and privilege history, scheduling attributes, namespace relative identifiers, mapped credentials, normalized and scaled processor times, fault counts and padded command text.

Extended accounting population converts accumulated memory time integrals into reported memory delay units, samples peak usage when the address space can be retained, and copies truncated input output counters with byte totals forced to zero when detailed byte tracking is disabled.

Group level accumulation folds a departing thread delay data, elapsed time, processor times and switch counts into shared group storage. The update proceeds only when shared storage is present and is serialized with interrupt state preserved.

Wire framing nests an identifier plus a statistics payload within an aggregate whose variant encodes process or group scope. Capacity planning covers identifier storage, aligned payload storage and container overhead, with group termination reserving twice the single record amount.

Group storage allocation reuses existing storage immediately and avoids creation for single member groups. Racing creators serialize so a single zeroed allocation becomes visible, with surplus allocations released.

Memory time integral maintenance applies only to user tasks possessing an address space and only after at least a tick of processor time elapsed since the prior refresh. Elapsed processor time scales resident and virtual sizes with a fixed downshift, performed with local interrupts masked.

Terminal failure handling moves through context validation, interrupt and atomic repair with diagnostics, repeated fault bounding, recursive exit diversion to a dead state, and finally normal exit delegation. Early stages halt rather than continue when context is interrupt handling or the idle task.

Thread and group termination entries accept a user status, retain only its low byte positioned as an exit code, and never return on success. One entry ends the caller while the other coordinates whole group shutdown before exiting.

Group termination coordination reuses a previously installed group code when present and suppresses status during exec handover. Otherwise it installs the requested code, marks group exiting and notifies surviving peers, resolving races under handler locking.

Peer termination enumeration resets group stop accounting, clears pending control state on initiator and peers, counts every peer, and for each still live peer queues unblockable termination and issues a wakeup. The result reports enumeration count.

Native wait entries cover info oriented collection plus legacy status collection by process, group or all descendants. Success is signaled positively with optional user publication of detailed info and resource usage, where publication faults become failures.

Compatibility wait entries preserve native collection semantics while translating resource usage according to time model width. Signal indication, info publication and user fault handling match native behavior across the boundary.

Child wake filtering combines eligibility under the active wait specification with a direct parenthood check when thread restricted waiting is selected. The queue callback forwards wakeups solely for matching children.

Wait setup validates requested options and event interests, resolves targets across all processes, single process, process group including caller group default, and descriptor backed process forms, checks identifier validity, acquires target references and inherits nonblocking mode from descriptor state.

Descriptor backed process resolution validates the supplied descriptor, obtains the associated process identity with a fresh reference, exposes descriptor status flags, and reports errors for empty or unassociated descriptors.

Kernel internal waiting separates preparation, collection and reference release. A transition to nonblocking without progress is converted to a retry indication, while the simplified helper focuses on exit collection for one process with optional status return.
Detailed wait result storage holds process number, owner number, collected status and cause code identifying the awaited transition class.

Wait request storage joins match type with referenced target, option flags, optional detailed info destination, optional usage destination, collected status slot, embedded child queue entry and a no task fallback error.
Fallback abort offers a weak termination hook that always faults and then halts if control somehow continues, serving environments without language level abort support.
Guard LINUX_WAITID_H marks the wait identifier definitions for single inclusion.

Handler lock siglock serializes parent notification checks with delivery, group exit code installation, lazy group storage publication and group accumulation. Notification and accumulation preserve interrupt state across the critical section while group control paths mask interrupts.

Listener traversal uses shared protection for cloning and delivery and exclusive protection solely for pruning refused entries. Integral refresh masks local interrupts across time sampling and accumulation.

Reference stability relies on task locking for address space sampling, read side critical sections for executable pointer plus identifier and credential translation, and reference acquisition that outlives each section.

Exception table handling tracks sort need with a boot flag, provides a dedicated mutex, sorts the main table once when required and nonempty, and resolves addresses by consulting kernel then module then accelerator tables and returning the earliest hit.

Invalid stop reason codes, termination from interrupt context, termination of the idle task, surpassing the repeated fault bound and entry to fallback abort all divert to fault or halt handling instead of normal return.

Allocation, construction, validation and user export failures abort their operation with an error and release partial state. Cases include buffer and attribute reservation, listener cloning, option and identifier validation, plus copying status, detailed info and usage to user memory.

Wait vocabulary includes event interests WEXITED plus WSTOPPED plus WCONTINUED, modifiers WNOHANG plus WNOWAIT plus __WNOTHREAD plus __WCLONE plus __WALL, and scopes P_ALL plus P_PID plus P_PGID plus P_PIDFD. Thread restriction additionally constrains wake matching to direct children.

Child state reasons CLD_CONTINUED plus CLD_STOPPED plus CLD_TRAPPED map respectively to continue signaling, low bits of group exit code and low bits of individual exit code under SIGCHLD. Accounting marks AXSIG plus ACORE plus ASU plus AFORK plus AGROUP record signal death, dumping, privilege, fork without exec and group completion.

Statistics protocol names TASKSTATS_CMD_NEW for creation events, TASKSTATS_TYPE_PID plus TASKSTATS_TYPE_TGID for identity scope, TASKSTATS_TYPE_AGGR_PID plus TASKSTATS_TYPE_AGGR_TGID for containers, TASKSTATS_TYPE_STATS for payload with TASKSTATS_TYPE_NULL alignment aid, and TASKSTATS_VERSION for record stamping.
Termination status encoding keeps the low eight user bits positioned as the process exit code, discarding higher bits of the supplied value.
